response.summary: The run completed as a valid, strictly executed delivery: the agent submitted explicitly after 2 decisions and 1 tool attempt, with no retries and no fixture faults. The selected candidate was the 'mean' baseline, the only observed candidate; its search validation error was 0.2361 (std 0.0835) and the sealed error was 0.2399, both above the 0.2 threshold, so quality_pass and scientific_success are false. All ridge candidates were untried, so no comparison among them is available.
findings: Valid delivery: verified_report reports valid=true, complete=true, termination='explicit_submit', fixture_faults=false, retries=0, and evaluation_reads=1.
Strict execution: strict_execution=true with 2 decisions, 1 tool attempt, 1 LLM request, and 1674 LLM tokens; active time was about 3.78 seconds.
Only one candidate was observed: 'mean' (fit_mean) succeeded with validation_mean=0.2361158964908156 and validation_std=0.08348837920905393.
All 12 ridge candidates (half/full fidelity, feature_grid 3 or 5, alpha 0.1/1/10) are marked untried with attempts=0 and null validation values; no ridge result was measured.
Quality did not pass: quality_pass=false and scientific_success=false, because the selected mean candidate's search validation error (0.2361) and sealed error (0.2399) both exceed the 0.2 threshold.
Provenance identifies the source as controlled_generated_regression on the demo split (instance 11, root_group 30000), i.e., controlled synthetic regression rather than scientific discovery.
No recovery was needed: retries=0 and no fixture faults were reported; the run ended by explicit submission rather than abstention or error.
The report records a data identity hash and model hash, but these are identifiers only and are not interpreted here as evidence of quality.
limitations: Only the mean baseline was observed; no ridge candidate was attempted, so no evidence exists about whether any ridge configuration would perform better or worse.
The sealed error (0.2399) is a single reported value with no uncertainty estimate; the validation std (0.0835) applies to the mean candidate's validation measurements, not to the sealed result.
The task is controlled synthetic regression on a demo split, so results do not constitute scientific discovery or evidence about real-world systems.
No information is available on why ridge candidates were left untried; this report does not infer causes beyond the recorded decision count and tool attempts.
No tuning guidance is offered, and nothing here should be used to tune against the sealed result.
